title: Refine information architecture, visual hierarchy, and content for deliver linked screen and diagram editing
summary: Turn the flagship journey into an implementation-ready information architecture, state map, content model, and accessible product-specific visual hierarchy.
acceptance_criteria: Map the complete information architecture required for `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save`.
Inventory current screens, states, actions, navigation, content, and hidden dependencies before proposing changes.
Identify the one primary action at each step and demote or progressively disclose secondary controls.
Define layout priorities for compact, standard, large, split-view, keyboard, and accessibility contexts as relevant.
Use repository-owned design tokens and components while preserving product-specific visual identity.
Define content hierarchy, terminology, button labels, help, error copy, and empty-state guidance.
Remove duplicated, contradictory, stale, or implementation-shaped user language.
Define loading, stale, offline, permission, error, partial, recovery, completion, and return states.
Ensure destructive, financial, hardware, privacy-sensitive, or externally visible actions are previewable and explicit.
Ensure focus order, semantics, touch targets, keyboard navigation, contrast, scaling, and reduced motion are designed from the start.
Define localization keys and grammatical context rather than translating screenshots after implementation.
Use representative real data and long localized strings in design review.
Define performance-sensitive surfaces and avoid visual structure that forces unnecessary rendering or data work.
Define what should remain outside the main journey and where it belongs.
Compare at least one credible alternative, including a simpler no-change or content-only option.
Record design decisions, rationale, evidence, uncertainty, and rejected alternatives.
Produce implementation-ready state maps and acceptance evidence, not only polished mockups.
Validate source-to-design traceability where HumbleStudio or repository exports exist.
Keep private or unreleased product evidence local and explicitly scoped.
Create proposed findings for unresolved product gaps.
Do not implement unrelated architecture or integration work in the design slice.
Validate design artifacts and leave zero app-owned warnings in supporting tooling.

agent_notes: Portfolio Human Validation & Product Launch Wave 13.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, sign, publish, enable billing or ads, operate hardware, write NAS data, migrate users, merge products, or create future game repositories.
Alternative considered and rejected: relying on internal confidence, green builds, or download counts without observed user or operator value would create false product certainty.
Research, telemetry, and feedback must remain privacy-safe, versioned, and optional where the product role requires it.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-after-sudoku`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Human validation remains valuable after the product implementation prerequisites and Sudoku priority.
